reason: The cited evidence shows that nanotwinning and phase transformations contribute to strength and ductility in specific HEAs/MEAs, but none of the passages demonstrate the dynamic, transient formation of nanoscale barriers under controlled loading as a general mechanism, nor do they support the specific temperature/strain-rate boundaries or the in situ formation of short-range ordered clusters.
premises: HEAs have inherently distorted, random solid-solution microstructures
Dynamic loading triggers transient nanoscale barriers (short-range order or twin networks) that pin dislocations
These barriers form in situ from local atomic rearrangements under stress
The barriers raise yield strength and work hardening while maintaining ductility
The mechanism operates at intermediate temperatures and moderate-to-high strain rates
